prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Select Your Ideal Desktop Companion Style", "Pick how active and social you want your companion to be during your work day.", "Focus Companion vs Playful Partner"]
1: ["Save Your Companion to Cloud", "Signing in preserves your companion's identity and memory safely across re-installs."]
2: ["Official Adoption Seal", "Finalize your pet's official records."]
3: ["Ready for Desktop Launch", "Watch your pet land on your screen and learn quick shortcut triggers.", "Watch Companion Spawn"]
4: ["Press Alt+P anytime to summon your pet to your main cursor."]
5: ["Secure Your Pet's Data & Memory", "Connect your account now so your pet's personality and progress are safely backed up.", "Your account links your pet's unique traits securely across updates."]
6: ["+ Unlock Rare Personality Trait"]
7: ["Use well-lit, front-facing photos for the crispest 3D pet generation."]
8: ["Creating Your Desktop Pet", "We'll send a system alert as soon as your companion is ready on screen."]
9: ["Your Desktop Companion is Active!", "Right-click your pet anytime to access settings, hide, or talk.", "Right click: Menu | Double click: Talk | Drag: Move position"]

verdicts.problem: Mentions unlocking a rare item, invoking scarcity or free extras
Asks for personal photos of the user
